steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.
In a medium sauce pan over medium heat, melt butter. Stir in ham and cook 1 minute. Stir in cream and heat through. Stir in Parmesan and cook until thick and smooth. Toss with cooked pasta.

raw_recipe.headline: Fettuccine Alfredo with Ham
raw_recipe.description: Cream and ham with Parmesan and a touch of butter.
raw_recipe.name: Fettuccine Alfredo with Ham

review.reviewBody: Excellent recipe. I tried it as is, and then tried it substituting Sour Cream for heavy cream, and liked that even better. I also added peas and fres muchrooms. Very yummy!
A very good recipe. A good sub for the very cream is evaporated milk which will make all alfredo recipes less costly and healthier without any sacrifice in taste.

This was terrific! I did as others had suggested and added diced onions and garlic to the ham. I would guess about three tablespoons of onion and one heaping teaspoon of garlic. The ham, onion, and garlic together reached the two cup line in my measuring cup before I heated them all together. I also only used 3/4 of the box of fettucine. The sauce could have handled the whole box, perhaps, but I thought it was just right this way. I would have tried either adding peas or mushrooms, but my picky 11 year old would have certainly turned up her nose at it then. After eating it, I think the mushrooms would be the way to go, although the recipe is great without them. Thank you for a terrific recipe that I will be making again. My fussy daughter even loved it, and that is saying alot! She hates to try new things.

This was very easy and tasty! I made the cream sauce just as the recipe states, but I also added some stuff. I sauteed garlic, mushrooms, the ham, and spinach with black pepper, italian seasoning, and basil. I also added an additional 1/2 of cheese (I used the 3 cheese blend) and 1/2 cup of pasta water. It was delicious but it made a ton!!!

Very, very easy and good! I used one pan for even easier clean-up. I boiled the pasta (as per others suggestions I reduced the amount of pasta. Also used shredded parmesan out of the can instead of grated) and while that was cooking I cut up the ham. After pasta was done, I drained and left in strainer then I used the same pan to cook the ham and then added the pasta back to the pan and heated thru. The ham/sauce doesn't take more than a few minutes. Sooo easy to throw together and on the table in 20 minutes. Very good! Thanks for the recipe!

This was a great recipe. I followed everything pretty closely, but used penne instead of fettuccine and added 1/4 diced onions to the saute pan with the ham. I also added 1/2 cup of frozen petite peas after tossing the pasta and the sauce. The heat transfer from the sauce and pasta heats the peas perfectly.

I added the most of the things that previous cooks recommended: 8 oz sliced baby portobello mushrooms, half a chopped sweet onion, 12 oz of pasta, freshly steamed baby peas, freshly grated parses an. I added the peas right at the end so as not to break the sauce. Amazing! Can't believe I made it!

Everyone loved this - especially my two picky preteen boys. The only adjustments I made the second time was 1 C. cream and 1/2 c. lite sour cream (thickens it up a little more). Oh - and some garlic. Easy, great recipe.

I substituted fat free 1/2 and 1/2 for heavy cream to lighten it up, and sauteed some shallots and garlic with the ham and threw frozen pea into the pasta water for last couple minutes of cooking time. Really good, family loved it, easy to put together, keeper!

Made it tonight for my hubby and I. It was delicious. I used 1/2 half & half cream and 1/2 sour cream for the sauce. I added sliced mushrooms, diced onions, diced red peppers along with diced ham. My hubby loved it and he can be a “picky” eater (a meat and potato guy)!

I did everything to this recipe that people hate. I changed it considerably. I used rotini pasta, half and half, and the green can parmesan (gasp!). I also added broccoli and cooked it with the pasta. But I needed a simple meal for just me tonight. This recipe was my jumping off point, and it was delicious!

None of the included images shows a Fettuccine pasta. Fettuccine is flat, thick noodles with a name meaning “little ribbons” in Italian. When I realized the #1 ingredient was wrong, I couldn't bring myself to try the recipe.
I changed the recipe entirely, added a bunch of stuff and removed a bunch of other stuff. Great recipe.
This is exactly what it claims to be. My only complaint is that it is very rich with a lot of fat. Needs something to cut that, like a white wine and a salad. I will likely make this again.
easy and yummy! I added broccoli to make it a complete meal that even the hubby and kids enjoyed!
made it and added the onion and garlic. it was delicious. excellent recipe to use up leftover ham
This was a very nice recipe. My whole family loved it and suggested next time I should add some mushrooms as well
Love this recipe! The only thing I added to it was sliced jalepenos (like the ones that come in a jar). That bit of spice combined with the creaminess of the pasta was a HUGE HIT with the family.

Amazing! I was asked to prepare dinner with some leftover ham... all I could come up with ham and scallops potatoes - ugh how boring! I went in search for some recipes and this one sounded delicious! And it was!

This was very good and very easy to make. I added about twice the amount of ham because there didn't seem to be much and increased the amount of alfredo as well. However, I reheated the leftovers the following day and it was very oily; couldn't really see the creamy part - but that's probably common with such an oil/cheese based recipe. Regardless, it tasted great from the pan.
